sections.html:
Clarence is in the northeastern part of Erie County, northeast of Buffalo, and it has no incorporated villages. The town covers 53.63 square miles, and the 2020 census counted 32,950 residents, a 7.4 percent increase over 2010. Tonawanda Creek forms the northern boundary with Niagara County, and Amherst, Lancaster and Newstead are the neighbors to the west, south and east.

In Clarence you can hire an agent, sell it yourself, or accept an offer from a direct buyer such as our company. The right choice turns on the house's condition, your timeline and whether past work was permitted.

A useful first step is a walk around the house with the permit list above in mind. Decks, sheds, pools, generators and a reroof are the projects that most often turn out to lack paperwork, and a Clarence buyer's attorney will look for exactly those. Knowing the answer before you call a direct buyer keeps the price from shifting later.

Clarence is a collection of hamlets rather than one downtown. Clarence Hollow is the main district in the southeast, Clarence Center sits near the middle of town around Goodrich Road and Clarence Center Road, and Harris Hill occupies the southwest corner. Swormville, Millersport and East Amherst lie along the western and northern borders and extend into neighboring towns. Spaulding Lake is an upscale housing project built around a former quarry north of Main Street, and Rock Oak Estates is a 55-plus community on Main Street.

Most of the town is in the Clarence Central School District. Part of the town falls in Williamsville Central instead, which makes the parcel the thing to verify.

  • The ZIP codes in town are 14031, 14032, 14051 and 14221.
  • New York Route 5 (Main Street) crosses the southern half of the town.
  • Transit Road (Route 78) marks the west line, and Sheridan Drive (Route 324) ends at Main Street.

sections.h2: How to challenge a Clarence assessment
sections.html:
Clarence assesses property at 100 percent of full market value and gives owners a three-step path to contest the number. The informal review accepts applications from January 1 to March 28. Bring reasonable evidence based on market sales, and compare like with like: a five-year-old house is not a fair match for a fifty-year-old one, and neither is a house in a different neighborhood.

Step two is a hearing before the Board of Assessment Review on Grievance Day, held the fourth Tuesday in May (May 25 in 2027). Use form RP-524 for that board only, not for the informal review. Owners who still disagree can ask for a small claims assessment review, and the town posts SCAR instructions and an assessment timetable on its assessment cycle page.

The town also runs an online Property Record Online System for looking up parcel data and the informal review worksheets, which become available after January 1. Check your record there for errors before you list.

The Town Clerk's office collects property tax in Clarence, from the Town Hall at One Town Place. Town and county bills go out by mid-January and are due on or about February 15. School bills go out by mid-September and are due on or about October 15. If your taxes are in escrow, you receive a receipt after the bank pays rather than a bill.

On May 1 a 7.5 percent penalty joins the levy, and 1.5 percent interest accrues monthly until unpaid taxes are sold in November, at which point the total reaches 18.78 percent. After June 30, unpaid town and county taxes move to Erie County Finance. School taxes carry a 7.5 percent penalty from October 16 to 31 and 9 percent in November, and unpaid school balances are re-levied onto the next town and county bill. The Clerk will take a partial payment in any amount.

If you sold a parcel, forward the bill to the new owner or call the Clerk so the office can locate them. Behind on taxes? The balance and any penalties are taken from your proceeds at closing, so ask the Clerk for the exact amount first.

Clarence requires permits for new construction, additions, conversions, pools, decks, sheds, walls, reroofing, and for plumbing, heating, cooling and electrical changes, including generators. Fence and sign permits come from Planning and Zoning, and driveway permits come from the County, State or Town Highway Department. The Building Department is at 6221 Goodrich Road, and the Town Clerk collects permit fees.

Work done without a required permit may hold up the sale of your property and may affect an insurance claim, and the town can issue a stop work order. Every permitted project needs inspections and a certificate of occupancy or compliance before the space is used.

  • Plumbers working in town need a license from the Town.
  • The town keeps records of permitted projects, and copies are available through a Freedom of Information request.
  • Planning and Zoning answers variance questions.

Ask the Building Department for the file on your address early. It shows which permits were closed, which are still open and whether a certificate of occupancy exists. If your file has gaps, request the records before you accept an offer, so a buyer can compare your paperwork to the house as it stands.

sections.h2: Recording a Clarence deed at the Erie County Clerk
sections.html:
The Erie County Clerk records deeds for Clarence parcels. Submit an original deed, signed and notarized, that carries a legal description and a street address for every party. P.O. boxes are not accepted. A TP-584 tax affidavit goes in duplicate, and an RP-5217 transfer report is prepared on the state's site because its barcode cannot be reused from another transaction.

Fees are a $45 statutory recording fee, $5 per page, $10 to file the TP-584, and $125 for the RP-5217 on residential or farm property ($250 for other property). The seller pays New York State and Erie County transfer tax at filing. The two shares add up to $4.50 per $500 of price.

An affidavit drops the rate to $2.00 per $500 for sellers aged 62 or older who have lived in and owned their one or two-family house for at least a year. A one percent mansion tax is added at $1 million or more. Residential transfers also need a Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership form delivered to the Clerk at the time of transfer, and the finished original deed is mailed back to you after indexing.

faqs.q: How many people live in Clarence, NY?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 32,950 residents, a 7.4 percent increase over the 2010 count of 30,673. Clarence has no incorporated villages.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Clarence?
faqs.a: The fourth Tuesday of May, so May 25 in 2027. File form RP-524 for the Board of Assessment Review, or go through the earlier informal review if you just want the Assessor to take a second look.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Clarence property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay the Town Clerk at One Town Place, Clarence, NY 14031, by check, cash, mail or online. After June 30 unpaid town and county taxes move to Erie County Finance.

faqs.q: Do unpermitted repairs affect selling a Clarence house?
faqs.a: They can. A missing permit can stall a sale, complicate an insurance claim and bring a stop work order. Ask the Building Department what a project needs to be closed out.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax in Erie County?
faqs.a: The combined State and Erie County rate is $4.50 per $500 of price, paid by the seller at filing. Eligible senior owners aged 62 or older can reduce it to $2.00 per $500.
